Shown offline: Init Seats replayed on 270 cases seats haiku in none and refuses no pair that ran before.
- THE JUDGE ORDER IS A TABLE (ASK 591; engine: Judge Order Read, Accept Build, Init Seats, Build Save Body; database: the tables `odv1_judge_order` and `odv1_judge_order_log`, six functions and three `dash_api` actions; dashboard: the Judge order tab; where it differs from any entry above in this section, this rule is right):
  - The table: `odv1_judge_order` holds one row per seat: seat (a model_config seat), list (panel or alternate) and ord (its place in that list). `odv1_judge_order_log` holds one row per save (saved_at, saved_by, before, after); the order's version is the highest log id. Both tables have row level security on and no grant to anon or authenticated.
  - The read: the node Judge Order Read (HTTP request to rpc `odv1_judge_order_read`, the credential of Write Tokens, run once, three tries, no error output) stands between each start path (Library Check, Dry Run Config) and Accept Models, so before any model call. It returns panel, alternate and version. The function raises "JUDGE ORDER: the order table could not be read (<fault>); no call was made" when the order fails a check below. Accept Build and Init Seats each throw "JUDGE ORDER: the order table could not be read (the read node gave no usable order); no call was made." when the read gave no two lists of seat names or a panel list of fewer than three. The code holds no fallback order.
  - The use: Accept Build `ORDER` and Init Seats `ORDER0` are the panel list followed by the alternate list; `__ALT` is the alternate list. Init Seats' output carries `judge_order` (version, panel, alternate). The rules of the drawing are as they were. A run reads the order once, at its start. A regrade enters by the same start path and draws its panel from the order as it stands at the regrade, not from the seats of the run it regrades.
  - The record: Build Save Body adds one line to review_notes: "[JUDGE ORDER v<n>: panel list <seats>; alternates list <seats> | SEATED: panel <seats>; reserve <seat or none>; alternates <seats>]". When the line cannot be built it is left out and the save goes on.
  - The checks (`odv1_judge_order_fault`, used by the read and by the save): the order is not empty; no seat stands twice; every seat has an active model_config row with role engine; the panel list holds at least three seats; every seat is named, in quotation marks, in the text of `odv1_record_panel_substitution` with its comments removed (the reserve recorder's seat list).
  - The save (`odv1_judge_order_save(p_panel, p_alt, p_by)`): it refuses, and changes nothing, unless the two lists hold exactly the seats the table holds now, each once, and every check passes; a seat is added or dropped only by its own ASK. A save rewrites the table and writes one log row with the order before and after; it returns the new version and the order. Its clearing of the table carries WHERE true, because the dashboard's database role runs with the safeupdate guard, which refuses a DELETE with no WHERE.
  - The page: the dashboard tab "Judge order" (judge591.js, loaded by patch.js after odv1.js) reorders each list, moves a seat between the lists, saves with a read-back, and shows the line-up a named pair of debaters would seat. Its `dash_api` actions: `judge_order` (`dash_judge_order`: the version, saved_at, and each seat with its list, place, model, family, active flag and fault-ledger state), `judge_order_save` (the save, saved_by "dashboard") and `judge_lineup` (`dash_judge_lineup(p_def, p_ch)`: panel, reserve, alternates, the fault-ledger-moved seats, each dropped seat with its reason, and the version). `dash_judge_lineup` is a copy of Init Seats' drawing and Resolve Seats' filters and holds its own copies of `NOT_PANEL`, the time-removed list, the family map and the OpenRouter seat list; a change to one of these in the engine must be made in it too. It cannot know which seats will accept the posture at a run's start.
  - Grants: EXECUTE on the six functions is held by postgres, service_role and lab_seat only; anon and authenticated reach them only through `dash_api`, which checks the passphrase. service_role and lab_seat can call the save directly; it makes the same checks whoever calls it.
  - Limits: not shown by a run; its mark is the first run's "[JUDGE ORDER v<n>" line in review_notes. Neither the page nor the review line names a single judge (§7); Init Seats still names the single_judge seat.
